syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Exploring Society India and Beyond Part-I

topics.title: When does Nature become a resource?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain when an element of Nature comes to be seen as a natural resource.
Apply the conditions of technological access, economic feasibility and cultural acceptability to decide whether something is a resource.

topics.title: Categories of natural resources by their use

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the resources without which life could not exist on Earth.
Recognise natural resources that humans turn into useful and beautiful objects.
Identify natural sources of energy and see that one resource can serve several uses.

topics.title: Renewable resources: restoration and regeneration

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between restoration and regeneration as principles of Nature.
Explain why renewable resources stay renewable only if Nature's rhythm is not disturbed.
Distinguish ecosystem functions from the ecosystem services humans receive.

topics.title: Non-renewable resources

concepts.learning_objective: Define non-renewable resources and identify examples such as fossil fuels and metals.
Suggest judicious uses of non-renewable resources and renewable substitutes.

topics.title: Distribution of natural resources and its implications

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the uneven distribution of resources shapes settlements, trade and industry.
Weigh the benefits of resource-based industries against costs such as displacement.
Explain why resources that cross political boundaries lead to sharing disputes.

topics.title: The 'Paradox of Plenty'

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of the natural resource curse or paradox of plenty.
Evaluate how investment in industry, skills and governance can overcome the resource curse.

topics.title: Stewardship: restoring and regenerating renewable resources

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the causes and effects of groundwater over-exploitation, as in Punjab.
Explain how traditional and organic practices restore soil health, as in Sikkim and Vrikshayurveda.
Describe the pollution caused by cement and the move towards alternative materials.

topics.title: Responsible and judicious use of resources

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the need to shift to renewable energy, with the International Solar Alliance as an example.
Evaluate fair access to resources and the idea of lokasangraha in acting as stewards of Nature.

topics.title: Rise and Fall of the Delhi Sultanate
topics.ncert_sections: Rise and Fall of the Delhi Sultanate

concepts.learning_objective: Name the five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in order and describe the instability of its successions.
Explain the campaigns of Ala-ud-din Khilji and the schemes of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
Describe Timur's attack on Delhi and its effect on the Sultanate.

topics.title: Resistance to the Delhi Sultanate
topics.ncert_sections: Resistance to the Delhi Sultanate

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Eastern Ganga kingdom under Narasimhadeva I resisted the Sultanate.
Explain the resistance of the Hoysalas and the Telugu chieftains in the south.
Identify the regional Sultanates and the Mewar kingdom as challenges to Delhi's power.

topics.title: The Vijayanagara Empire
topics.ncert_sections: The Vijayanagara Empire; Krishnadevaraya

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the founding of Vijayanagara and its rivals in the Deccan.
Explain the military and cultural achievements of Krishnadevaraya's reign.
Analyse the effects of the Battle of Talikota on the Vijayanagara Empire.

topics.title: The Mughals
topics.ncert_sections: The Mughals; Akbar; Aurangzeb

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Babur's victory at Panipat founded the Mughal Empire.
Explain the military and political strategies Akbar used to expand and stabilise his empire.
Describe the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb and the causes of Mughal decline.

topics.title: Resistance to the Mughals: Peasants, Tribes and Rajputs
topics.ncert_sections: Resistance to the Mughals; Surge of the Rajputs

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the resistance of peasant communities, tribal groups and Rani Durgavati.
Explain how Rajput rulers such as Maharana Pratap resisted Mughal dominance.

topics.title: The Ahoms and the Rise of the Sikhs
topics.ncert_sections: The Ahoms; The Rise of the Sikhs

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the paik system and how the Ahoms defended their independence.
Describe how the Sikh Gurus responded to persecution and the founding of the Khalsa.

topics.title: Administering India
topics.ncert_sections: Administering India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of the sultan and the iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate.
Identify the duties of Akbar's ministers and the division of the empire into subahs.
Explain the mansabdari system and Todar Mal's revenue reforms.

topics.title: People's Lives
topics.ncert_sections: People's Lives; Temples as centres of economic activity

concepts.learning_objective: Describe agriculture, crafts and trade in the period and the condition of common people.
Explain how the hundi system helped merchants trade across political boundaries.
Describe the economic role of temples in this period.

topics.title: Who Are the Marathas?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the homeland, language and early rulers of the Marathas.
Explain how the bhakti saints of Maharashtra built the cultural foundation for Maratha power.

topics.title: Foundation of Maratha Power and the Rise of Chhatrapati Shivaji

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Chhatrapati Shivaji's early life, his first campaigns and the founding of the navy.
Explain how guerrilla warfare and surprise raids helped the Marathas defeat bigger armies.
Describe the sacking of Surat and what it shows about Chhatrapati Shivaji's conduct.

topics.title: Purandar, Agra, Coronation and the Conquest of the South

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the treaty of Purandar and Chhatrapati Shivaji's escape from Agra.
Explain the significance of Chhatrapati Shivaji's coronation at Raigad in 1674.
Analyse why the conquest of the South gave the Marathas strategic depth.

topics.title: The Marathas after Chhatrapati Shivaji

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the course of the Mughal-Maratha wars after Chhatrapati Shivaji's death.
Explain the rise of the Peshwas and the pan-Indian expansion of the Marathas.
Evaluate why the British are said to have taken India mainly from the Marathas.

topics.title: Maratha Administration: Civilian Administration and Revenue

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the council of eight ministers and the role of each minister.
Explain the features and values of Chhatrapati Shivaji's civilian administration.
Calculate and explain the taxes chauth and sardeshmukhi.

topics.title: Military Administration, Maritime Supremacy, Justice and Trade

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the divisions of the Maratha army and the importance of forts.
Explain how the Maratha navy challenged European naval control.
Describe the Maratha judicial system and their trade networks.

topics.title: Cultural Revival, Maratha Women, Thanjavur and the Maratha Legacy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Chhatrapati Shivaji's cultural policies and the ideal of Swarajya shaped the Maratha legacy.
Describe the contributions of Tarabai and Ahilyabai Holkar.
Describe the cultural contributions of the Thanjavur Marathas, especially Serfoji II.

topics.title: The Age of Colonialism
topics.ncert_sections: The Age of Colonialism

concepts.learning_objective: Define colonialism and place the European 'Age of Colonialism' in its longer history.
Identify the political, economic, religious and scientific motives behind European expansion.
Evaluate the colonisers' claim of a 'civilising mission' against its actual results.

topics.title: Europeans in India: the Portuguese, the Dutch and the French
topics.ncert_sections: Europeans in India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe India's economic standing in the world before European colonisation.
Explain how the Portuguese combined commercial control with religious persecution and faced resistance.
Compare the aims and fortunes of the Dutch and the French in India.

topics.title: Enter the British: from traders to rulers
topics.ncert_sections: Enter the British; From traders to rulers; The strategy of 'divide and rule'

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the 'divide and rule' strategy using the Battle of Plassey as an example.
Explain the Doctrine of Lapse and why it caused resentment.
Analyse how the subsidiary alliance transferred real power and costs to Indian rulers.

topics.title: From Paradise to Hell? Famines and the drain of wealth
topics.ncert_sections: From Paradise to Hell?; Devastating famines; The drain of India's wealth

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how colonial revenue and trade policies worsened famines in India.
Describe the drain of India's wealth and the scholars who documented it.

topics.title: Changing Landscapes: industries and governance
topics.ncert_sections: Decline of India's indigenous industries; Dismantling traditional governance structures

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how British trade policies ruined India's indigenous industries, especially textiles.
Describe India's village self-governance and how British rule and law replaced it.

topics.title: Changing Landscapes: education and the economy
topics.ncert_sections: Transforming Indian education; Reshaping economic structures to serve imperial needs

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the aims and effects of Macaulay's 1835 Minute on Indian Education.
Analyse how railways and the colonial economy served British interests and were paid for by Indians.

topics.title: Early resistance movements
topics.ncert_sections: Early Resistance Movements: Challenging Colonial Authority

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Sannyasi-Fakir rebellion and its later influence.
Explain why tribal communities such as the Kols and Santhals rose against colonial rule.
Explain the causes and outcome of the Indigo Revolt.

topics.title: The Great Rebellion of 1857 and the legacy of colonialism
topics.ncert_sections: The Great Rebellion of 1857; The Legacy of European Colonialism in India

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the causes of sepoy discontent leading to the 1857 rebellion.
Explain the course, failure and significance of the Great Rebellion of 1857.
Evaluate the intended and unintended consequences of colonial rule in India.

chapters.title: Universal Franchise and India’s Electoral System

topics.title: Universal Adult Franchise: meaning and importance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what universal adult franchise means and who is entitled to vote in India.
Evaluate why the Constitution makers granted universal franchise from the time of Independence.

topics.title: Bridging barriers and enabling participation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how India's size and diversity make organising elections a complex task.
Identify the measures taken by the ECI to remove barriers to voting.

topics.title: A class election: the election process in miniature

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of the election officer and the importance of a secret ballot.
Interpret election results, invalid votes and the NOTA option.

topics.title: The Election Commission of India and the Model Code of Conduct

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure of the ECI and the tasks it performs.
Identify the purpose of the Model Code of Conduct and recognise its violations.

topics.title: Managing the electoral process: polling, EVMs and VVPAT

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the steps a voter goes through at a polling station.
Explain the use of EVMs and VVPAT and the reservation of Lok Sabha seats.

topics.title: Elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the First-Past-the-Post system to decide the winner of a constituency.
Distinguish between MPs and MLAs and explain how governments are formed.

topics.title: Indirect elections: Rajya Sabha, President and Vice President

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how members of the Rajya Sabha are chosen and why it is a permanent house.
Identify the electoral colleges that elect the President and the Vice President.

topics.title: Challenges and the road ahead

concepts.learning_objective: Identify challenges such as money power, criminalisation and voter apathy.
Evaluate the role of an informed and vigilant voter in strengthening democracy.

chapters.title: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive

topics.title: Introduction and composition of the Parliament
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Composition of the Parliament of India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the composition of the Indian Parliament and explain why India chose a bicameral system.
Distinguish the direct election of Lok Sabha members from the indirect election of Rajya Sabha members.
Identify the presiding officers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha and their role.

topics.title: Legislative functions: constitutional functions and lawmaking
topics.ncert_sections: Legislative Functions of the Parliament: 1) Constitutional function, 2) Lawmaking

concepts.learning_objective: State the constitutional functions of Parliament and the core constitutional values it upholds.
Explain the steps by which a bill becomes an act, using the example of the RTE Act, 2009.
Explain the special rules for introducing a Money Bill.

topics.title: Executive and financial accountability
topics.ncert_sections: 3) Executive accountability; 4) Financial accountability

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Question Hour holds ministers accountable to the Lok Sabha.
Describe how standing committees scrutinise the work of ministries.
Explain how Parliament approves and monitors government expenditure through the budget.

topics.title: Executive functions: the President, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers
topics.ncert_sections: Executive Functions of Parliament; Differences Between the Legislature and the Executive

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the President as Head of State and nominal head of the Executive, including discretionary powers.
Explain the role of the Prime Minister and the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers.
Distinguish the functions of the Legislature from those of the Executive.

topics.title: The Judiciary: checks and balances
topics.ncert_sections: The Judiciary - Role of Checks and Balances

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Judiciary's role in interpreting laws and guarding the Constitution.
Explain how the separation of powers and checks and balances stop any one organ from becoming too powerful.

topics.title: Legislature and executive at the state level
topics.ncert_sections: Legislative and Executive Functions at the State Level; Union, State and Concurrent Lists; Structure of State Legislatures

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Union, State and Concurrent Lists and which government can legislate on each.
Compare the parallel structures of the Union and State governments.
Distinguish unicameral and bicameral state legislatures and name states with a Vidhan Parishad.

topics.title: Challenges to the effective functioning of the legislatures
topics.ncert_sections: Challenges to the Effective Functioning of the Legislatures

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret data on sessions, sittings and productivity of the legislature.
Evaluate how informed and engaged citizens can strengthen the legislature.

topics.title: Introduction: factors of production and land
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Factors of Production; Land (natural resources)

concepts.learning_objective: Define factors of production and name the four types along with technology as a facilitator.
Explain that land in economics includes all natural resources used in production.

topics.title: Labour, human capital and its facilitators
topics.ncert_sections: Labour (human resources); People as a resource; Facilitators of human capital

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish labour as effort from human capital as the skills and quality of that effort.
Explain how education, training, healthcare and work culture build human capital.

topics.title: Challenges to human capital and India's ancient skill heritage
topics.ncert_sections: Challenges to human capital; India's ancient skill heritage

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse challenges to human capital and the conditions for a demographic dividend.
Describe India's traditional skill systems such as the shilpa shastras and stitched shipbuilding.

topics.title: Capital
topics.ncert_sections: Capital

concepts.learning_objective: Identify capital as money plus human-made durable assets used in production.
Explain how businesses raise capital through savings, bank loans and the stock market.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship
topics.ncert_sections: Entrepreneurship

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the tasks of an entrepreneur, including taking risks and combining factors.
Explain what a startup is and why entrepreneurs such as J.R.D. Tata served society.

topics.title: Technology: an enabler of production
topics.ncert_sections: Technology: An Enabler of Production

concepts.learning_objective: Explain technology as applied scientific knowledge and how it changes production.
Explain how platforms like SWAYAM and National Career Service widen access to skills and jobs.

topics.title: How the factors are connected and responsibilities towards them
topics.ncert_sections: How are the Factors Connected?; Responsibilities towards Factors of Production

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how factors combine in different proportions in labour- and capital-intensive production.
Explain what a supply chain is and how its disruption can halt production.
Describe producers' responsibilities to the environment and workers, including CSR.
